mechanism_narrative: A historically low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS = 0.09%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 235.0 indicates rising inflation, which triggers a monetary tightening cycle that reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 235.0 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous expansion in private employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) above historical thresholds (PAYEMS > 138000 and RSAFS > 430000) signals robust consumer demand, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS > 138000 and RSAFS > 430000 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 5.5%) characterizes a late-cycle expansion, where tight labor markets drive wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 5.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: An industrial production level above 102.5 (INDPRO > 102.5) indicates strong manufacturing output, signaling robust corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO > 102.5 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1070 (HOUST > 1070) signal strong consumer confidence and immediate economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST > 1070 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 6.0%) indicates a tightening labor market, which typically precedes positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 6.0% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.1% (FEDFUNDS > 0.1%) indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
